threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You know you’re a newcomer when you still think catching the bus is faster than the Tube. The locals have that ‘train versus bus’ debate down to an art.
Last week on the 208, a guy brought a saxophone, played R&B the whole ride. Everyone forgot we were tired; it turned into an impromptu concert.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you hear three languages at the bakery and somehow know exactly which loaf each regular wants— that’s when you feel at home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a kebab shop that turns into a techno club at midnight, complete with a dance floor made of old tiles.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell the locals by how they casually shrug off BART delays, while newcomers are still fumbling with their Clipper cards.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 5 tonight, driver had to stop because a guy set up a full picnic on the seats. Classic. Only in SF would someone prioritize brunch on Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the 'Vila de Gràcia' fiestas are just about the fireworks. It's really about the community coming together, not just the spectacle.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the metro map; they still stare at it like it's an ancient treasure map.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still wait for the Tube to be on time. We know it’s a fantasy. Locals roll their eyes and plan for delays like it’s part of the day.
Caught the N59 last night; a guy was serenading the whole bus with classic R&B, and surprisingly, everyone joined in. Best late-night vibe ever.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When you see a street vendor selling homemade kebabs next to a protest for better public transport. That's Neukölln for you, always juggling flavors and voices.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can find a random open-air cinema in a former car park, where locals set up picnic blankets and share homemade snacks. Pure Berlin vibe.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only true locals know to walk half a block around the Civic Center to avoid the BART chaos when there's a delay. Visitors just stand there, perplexed.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni delayed today because a dog decided the tracks were its new favorite sunbathing spot. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think every bar serves tapas, but many locals just grab a sandwich from the bakery. The real snack scene hides in the back streets.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You’ll catch them standing cluelessly at the metro ticket machines, pressing buttons like it's a game show. Locals know to just hop on.
